chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, and Ahmad ibn Abdoon informed me of through the previously mentioned chain: from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim and Amr ibn Uthman, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from one who heard it from al-'Abd al-Salih عليه السلام: concerning

A woman, when she becomes pure from menstruation and has not touched water, her husband should not have intercourse with her until she performs ghusl (ritual bath). But if he does so, there is no harm in it. And he said: "That she touch water is more beloved to me."

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: more beloved or preferable to me
key_terms.تَمَسَّ الْمَاءَ: to use water, meaning to perform ritual washing
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Can a husband have intercourse with his wife after menstruation ends but before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who has become pure from menstruation but has not yet performed ghusl (ritual bath). It indicates that her husband should wait until she performs ghusl, while also stating that if intercourse occurs before that, there is no harm, with preference given to washing first.
